summary: Full text of the 2022 Adv Nutr dose-response meta-analysis (22 RCTs, oral L-arginine 2-30 g/day) shows lower SBP (-6.40 mmHg) and DBP (-2.64 mmHg) with very high heterogeneity and no benefit above 9 g/day; it gets the record's one eligible context for Cardiovascular/Heart Health. The sports meta-analysis includes excluded arginine forms (AAKG, aspartate) and a heterogeneous aerobic estimate, so it gets no credit; Dong 2011 is abstract-only and overlaps 34967840. A new applicability block limits credit to BP (cardiovascular).

applicability.studied_population: Adults (healthy or with cardiometabolic conditions or pre-eclampsia) given oral L-arginine 2-30 g/day for 4-180 days in 22 placebo-controlled RCTs.

identity.preparation: Oral L-arginine in 22 placebo-controlled trials; one included trial (Willoughby 2011) used arginine alpha-ketoglutarate and one (Facchinetti 2007) began with 5 days of IV arginine before oral dosing.

population.description: 22 RCTs (30 effect sizes), adults aged 20-64 (431 L-arginine, 394 placebo for SBP): healthy adults and people with hypertension, hypercholesterolemia, type 2 diabetes, peripheral arterial disease, coronary disease, heart failure, PCOS, pre-eclampsia or high pre-eclampsia risk in pregnancy; baseline SBP 108-151 mmHg.

study_contexts.study_design: PROSPERO-registered (CRD42021242772) systematic review and random-effects dose-response meta-analysis of oral L-arginine placebo-controlled RCTs lasting >=4 days; infusion-only, acute, and vitamin/mineral-combination studies excluded; Cochrane risk of bias and GRADE.

dose.administration_frequency: Trial-specific daily oral regimens (Table 2); no single pooled schedule.
dose.reported_regimen: Daily L-arginine 2-30 g for 4-180 days (Results; Table 2 lists 2-24 g/d arms). Subgroup without benefit above 9 g/d; nonlinear model suggested SBP effect at >=4 g/d. No scalar pooled dose.

normalization.basis: Descriptive trial ranges; no minimum effective dose, ceiling or label benchmark is asserted.

co_therapies: Some arms combined L-arginine with a hypocaloric diet and exercise (Lucotti 2006) or an oral contraceptive (Battaglia 2010), matched in placebo arms; background cardiometabolic medication varied by population.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC9340976 article page): Methods (Study selection, Data extraction, Statistics), Results (study selection, Table 2 characteristics, SBP/DBP pooled effects, Table 3 subgroups, REMR dose-response, meta-regression), Table 1 risk of bias, reference list 11-56.

outcomes.name: No significant SBP reduction with >9 g/d, duration >24 days or obese participants; DBP not reduced with >9 g/d, in males or obese participants; publication bias considerable for DBP.

limitations: Very high heterogeneity; many small trials, several in pregnancy/pre-eclampsia or disease populations; benefit absent in some subgroups (>9 g/d, >24 days, obesity). A surrogate BP effect, not cardiovascular-event prevention.
Included-study identity verified from the source reference list: 20 PMIDs; de Lima 2012 (Portuguese) and Malfatti 2014 have no PMID in the source and none is invented.

Willoughby 2011 tested arginine alpha-ketoglutarate, which this record does not cover; Facchinetti 2007 began with IV arginine despite the stated infusion exclusion. Dosage forms are not tabulated; recorded as trial-specific oral preparations.

identity.name: Arginine interventions; other-supplement combinations excluded from this source.

population.description: 18 controlled trials in athletes and physically active adults (judo, wrestling, soccer, cycling, resistance-trained, active), mostly young men; 15 meta-analysed.

study_contexts.study_design: PRISMA/PICOS systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis (Hedges' g) of randomized placebo-controlled parallel or crossover trials; multi-ingredient supplements excluded; outcomes split into aerobic (<=VO2max) and anaerobic (>VO2max) tests.

outcomes.name: Anaerobic performance SMD 0.24 (95% CI 0.05-0.43), p=0.01, I2 0%; aerobic performance SMD 0.84 (0.12-1.56), p=0.02, I2 89% with funnel-plot asymmetry (Egger p<0.05).
Most individual trials showed no difference for individual performance measures (Table 2).

limitations: Do not infer general vascular, erectile or nonexercise benefit from these exercise tests.
Source recommendations require source/trial-specific context; no new dose threshold is created here.

dose.administration_frequency: Acute single doses 30 min to 4 h before testing, or chronic daily dosing for 7-56 days (Table 1).
co_therapies: Exercise protocols and placebo conditions matched within trials.
dose.reported_regimen: Absolute 1.5-12 g/day (6 g/day in 8 studies) or 0.075-0.15 g/kg body mass; acute or 7 days to 8 weeks. Supplement types: L-arginine (15 studies), arginine aspartate (1), arginine alpha-ketoglutarate (2).

normalization.basis: A heterogeneous synthesis has no single assigned-arm dose. Descriptive regimens do not create an intake recommendation, equivalent preparation or efficacy threshold.

source_provenance.location: Full text (PMC7282262): Methods 2.1-2.4, Table 1 (supplement type, dose, timing), Table 2 (study rows), Results (Figures 5-6 text), Funding/COI.

clinical_review.notes: No independent credit: full text not open access, so included trials and regimens are not verified here; its trials are largely carried into the 2022 meta-analysis (34967840), which holds the credit.

source_provenance.location: PubMed abstract only (Am Heart J; not open access).

limitations: Dong 2011 abstract: 11 double-blind placebo-controlled RCTs, 387 participants, oral L-arginine 4-24 g/d; SBP -5.39 mmHg (-8.54 to -2.25), DBP -2.66 (-3.77 to -1.54). Consistent with 34967840 but not counted separately; not a finding that the source is invalid.
